column1: 1,General non-tech,Basic,Please introduce yourself and tell the panel briefly what your study is about.,"""Thank you, Professor. My name is ... and I am presenting my MSc thesis, Machine Learning Survival Prediction for ICU Patients with Non-Communicable Diseases. The study asks a simple design question: when we build a survival model for ICU patients with an NCD, should we train it on all ICU patients, on NCD patients only, or start from the general model and adapt it to NCD patients through transfer learning? I compared the three approaches on MIMIC-IV, using Cox, random survival forest and XGBoost, all tested on the same held-out group of NCD patients.""","Warm and composed. Smile, keep it under one minute and end on the question your study answers.","""I will keep the introduction short so we have more time for questions."" (This one you should never fail; rehearse it until it is automatic.)",,"E

NCDs cause about three in four deaths not linked to COVID-19, and many of these patients end up in intensive care. I wanted to know whether that habit actually serves NCD patients, because it affects how hospitals, including those in low- and middle-income countries, choose prediction tools.""","Genuine and personal, but brief. One fact, one observation, one reason.","Not applicable: this is about you. If your mind goes blank, say: ""Let me give the practical reason first,"" and state the gap.",,"E

column1: 5,General non-tech,Basic,What were your main objective and your specific objectives?,"""My main objective was to compare the predictive performance of general, disease-specific and transfer learning survival models for one-year survival among ICU patients with NCDs, using MIMIC-IV. column1: 7,General non-tech,Intermediate,How did you identify the research gap?,"""I read three bodies of work. First, general ICU mortality models, which are mostly trained on all patients. Second, disease-specific models for heart failure, sepsis, stroke and cancer, which report results only within their own disease group. Third, the small transfer learning literature, such as Xu and colleagues on eICU, which used single diagnoses and a yes-or-no outcome. None of them compared all three approaches for NCD patients with a survival outcome on a common held-out group. That intersection is the gap.""","Methodical. Show that the gap came from reading, not from assumption.","""I cannot claim to have read every paper in the field, so I phrase it as no identified study, based on my search of the databases I listed in Chapter 2.""",,"E

column1: 9,General non-tech,Intermediate,"What ethical issues did your study raise, and how did you deal with them?","""Thank you. The data are real patient records, even though they are de-identified. I completed the PhysioNet credentialing and training and signed the data use agreement. I kept all patient-level data and trained models on my own machine, never on GitHub, because models can memorise records. Only aggregate tables and figures were shared. I also report that survival predictions should support, not replace, clinical judgement, because a poor prognosis estimate could influence end-of-life decisions.""","Serious and responsible. Ethics questions reward calm, concrete answers.","""I am not sure of the exact institutional procedure for that point; I followed the PhysioNet agreement and my university's guidance, and I would confirm the rest with the ethics office.""",,"E

column1: 11,General non-tech,Intermediate,"What was the biggest challenge you faced, and how did you overcome it?","""The biggest challenge was changing direction mid-way. I first built binary in-hospital mortality models, and my supervisor advised moving to survival analysis, which is a better fit for the question. I kept the cohort and predictor pipeline, relabelled the earlier outputs as legacy, and rebuilt the outcome and models around time to death. A practical challenge was the size of the MIMIC-IV event tables, which I handled by filtering them once with DuckDB and caching the result.""","Honest and solution-focused. Examiners like hearing how you recovered, not how hard it was.","""There were several; the one that taught me most was ..."" Pick any real one rather than freezing.",,"E

For each one I describe the mitigation in Section 1.8: full cohort reporting, a documented missing-data method, and results reported per NCD group.""","Calm and non-defensive. column1: 16,General non-tech,Advanced,How would you convince a sceptical policy maker that your findings matter?,"""I would talk in terms of choices and cost. Every hospital that adopts a prediction tool must decide whether one general model is enough or whether NCD patients need their own. My study gives evidence for that decision. If a general or adapted model performs as well as a separate one, a health system saves the cost of building and maintaining extra models. If not, it knows where investment is justified.""","Persuasive but grounded.
